Today you make a 5-minute talk from the Nebraska yield data used in Ex-2-1. The AI builds the slides; you decide what the talk says and to whom, and you judge the deck as the audience will see it.

**Rules:**

A. Decide the audience, the message and the outline **before** you ask the AI for slides.

B. Keep the requests you actually sent in this file, with the blanks filled in.

C. You judge the deck by rendering it and stepping through it, not by reading the chat window.

# The numbers for the talk

Read the data, then compute the number of counties and the average yield in each year, rounded to whole bushels per acre.

```{r}
#| label: facts
yields <- read_csv(here::here("data", "2-1-nebraska-yield.csv"), show_col_types = FALSE)

yields |>
  group_by(year) |>
  summarise(counties = n(), average_yield = round(mean(corn_yield)))
```

# Task 3: Ask the AI for the deck

**My request to the AI.** Fill in every `<...>` from Tasks 1 and 2, then send it:

```text
Make a revealjs deck at analysis/talk.qmd from the data in
data/2-1-nebraska-yield.csv (one row per county and year, with the
corn yield in bushels per acre). The audience is <who, and what they
already know>. I have <number> minutes. The message: <one sentence>.

Slides, in order, with these titles:
<numbered list: each title as a sentence, and what the slide shows>

Hide all code. The sentence above each chunk that the last paragraph
asks for goes in the speaker notes of that slide, not on the slide.
Numbers on slides rounded to whole bushels per acre, written as inline
R. Add a last slide titled "Checks", after the final slide, with the
checks: number of rows (I expect <number>) and the years covered (I
expect <first year> to <last year>). Use embed-resources: true.

Put the code in my Quarto document analysis/talk.qmd, under the
heading "<the title of your first slide>", as R code chunks. Above
each chunk, write one plain-English sentence saying what it does and
why. Build every path with here::here(); no setwd(), no absolute paths.
Print each check on its own line as "name of check: expected X, got Y".
Render the document to HTML.
```
